priority.when: Always use first to find performance-related code, configurations, and existing optimization patterns
priority.why: Semantic search helps identify performance bottlenecks, caching implementations, and monitoring setups more effectively than keyword searches.

priority.when: After identifying relevant files, examine their contents to understand current performance implementations and identify optimization opportunities
priority.why: Full context is essential for making informed performance optimization decisions and avoiding unintended side effects.

priority.when: Execute performance profiling tools, load testing commands, and monitoring setup scripts
priority.why: Command-line tools are essential for performance analysis, benchmarking, and system-level optimizations that require external tooling.

priority.when: Use performance monitoring and analysis tools through MCP servers for advanced insights and integrations
priority.why: MCP tools provide specialized performance analysis capabilities and real-time data from external monitoring systems.

priority.when: Make targeted performance optimizations to code, configurations, and documentation files
priority.why: Apply diff is the primary tool for implementing performance improvements while maintaining code quality and consistency.

tool.name: codebase_search
tool.purpose: Find performance-related code, configurations, and existing optimization patterns
tool.when_to_use: At the beginning of performance analysis to understand current implementation

syntax.command: Use semantic search queries to find performance bottlenecks, caching implementations, database queries, and monitoring setups

parameter.name: query
parameter.description: Natural language query describing performance issues or optimization needs
parameter.example: "slow database queries causing high response times"

example.code: codebase_search "N+1 query optimization slow response time database performance"
example.output: Finds files with database queries, performance-related configurations, and existing optimization patterns

tool.name: read_file
tool.purpose: Examine specific performance implementations and configurations
tool.when_to_use: When analyzing specific files identified through codebase_search or when detailed code review is needed

syntax.command: Read the complete contents of performance-related files

parameter.name: path
parameter.description: Path to the file to read

example.output: Provides complete monitoring configuration for analysis and improvement recommendations

tool.name: command
tool.purpose: Execute performance profiling and testing commands
tool.when_to_use: When running performance analysis tools, load tests, or setting up monitoring infrastructure

syntax.command: Execute performance-related command-line tools and scripts

example.output: Executes configured load test to measure system performance under various conditions

tool.name: mcp
tool.purpose: Access performance monitoring and analysis tools through MCP servers
tool.when_to_use: When specialized performance analysis tools are available through MCP servers for advanced insights

syntax.command: Use MCP tools for performance analysis and monitoring

parameter.name: server_name
parameter.description: Name of the MCP server providing performance tools

parameter.name: tool_name
parameter.description: Specific performance analysis tool to use

parameter.name: arguments
parameter.description: Arguments for the performance analysis tool

example.output: Uses specialized performance analysis tool to identify bottlenecks and optimization opportunities

tool.name: apply_diff
tool.purpose: Implement performance optimizations in code and configuration files
tool.when_to_use: When making specific performance improvements identified through analysis or testing

syntax.command: Apply targeted changes to optimize performance while maintaining code quality

parameter.name: path
parameter.description: Path to the file to modify

parameter.name: diff
parameter.description: Changes to apply to the file
parameter.example: <search> <start_line>15</start_line> <end_line>25</end_line> <content>SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?</content> <replacement> <start_line>15</start_line> <end_line>25</end_line> <content>SELECT id, name, email FROM users WHERE email = ? AND status = 'active'</content> </replacement> </search> <add> <start_line>30</start_line> <end_line>35</end_line> <content>-- Add index on email and status for query optimization</content> </add> </diff>

example.output: Optimizes database query by adding specific index and improving WHERE clause for better performance
